title: One request id from edge to every hop
asA: support engineer holding a single id from a bug report
iWant: that id assigned or accepted at the edge, echoed to the client, and threaded through every downstream call
soThat: one identifier retrieves the complete story of one user action

acceptanceCriteria.description: A request arriving with a valid X-Request-Id keeps it: the same value appears in the response header and in every request-scoped log line.
acceptanceCriteria.when: the response and logs are inspected
acceptanceCriteria.then: the inbound value is echoed in the response and present on every request-scoped log line

acceptanceCriteria.description: A request arriving without X-Request-Id is assigned one at the edge before any other middleware runs, and the assigned value is echoed in the response.
acceptanceCriteria.then: a generated id in the documented format is present in the response header

acceptanceCriteria.description: An inbound X-Request-Id failing the documented format or length constraints is replaced with a generated id rather than propagated, so hostile header values never flow into logs and downstream systems.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a request with an oversized or malformed X-Request-Id
acceptanceCriteria.when: the response and logs are inspected
acceptanceCriteria.then: a fresh generated id is used and the malformed inbound value is not propagated

acceptanceCriteria.description: Every downstream call made on behalf of a request carries the request id onward in its headers or protocol equivalent.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a handler calling a downstream HTTP dependency
acceptanceCriteria.then: it carries the same X-Request-Id value

acceptanceCriteria.description: Error responses carry the request id in both the response header and the problem-details instance field, so a failure report contains its own correlation handle.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a request ending in an error
acceptanceCriteria.then: the header and the envelope's instance field both carry the request id
